newsitem.title: USA: US files WTO challenge on food-trade barriers.
newsitem.headline: US files WTO challenge on food-trade barriers.

text.p: The United States filed challenges in the World Trade Organization against Japanese and Philippine practices that impede U.S. meat and produce exports, Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky announced.
Japan imposes "needless" variety-by-variety testing standards that block large-scale sales of fruit and vegetables, Barshefsky said.
The Philippines was accused of dragging its feet on promises to open its market to U.S. pork and poultry.
Barshefsky said the United States invoked the WTO's dispute settlement procedures against the two nations. For months, she had threatened WTO action over the disputes.

The Philippines agreed to the U.S. request for consultations over its commitment to allow a minimum level of pork and meat imports through use of a tariff-rate quota. Consultations were expected to begin by May 1.
In a statement, Barshefsky said the Philippines has failed to issue any import licenses for 1997 and that its licensing system gave most licenses to domestic producers uninterested in imports.
Apple sales have been a salient issue in the dispute over Japan's variety-by-variety testing requirements.

"Japan's requirement that several years be spent duplicating tests for each addtional variety is without quarantine significance, blocks market access and ignores available scientific evidence which demonstrates the efficacy of existing quarantine treatments for a commodity," Barskefsky said.
WTO consultations with Japan should be held by May 7, Barshefsky's office said.
The U.S. has taken 25 complaints to WTO dispute settlement in the past 24 months, nine involve agriculture and fishery products.
